clinician.final_diagnosis: Metastatic methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection with infective endocarditis, pulmonary septic emboli, axillary abscess with a subacute presentation in a patient with chronic end-stage kidney disease on maintenance haemodialysis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A male patient in his 40s with end-stage diabetic nephropathy on maintenance haemodialysis presented with intermittent low to moderate-grade fever, generalized weakness, night sweats, exertional breathlessness, mild cough, and recent left axillary pain. Ultrasound demonstrated a left axillary abscess that was aspirated. Cultures from the abscess grew methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Echocardiography revealed multiple vegetations on the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve consistent with infective endocarditis. Although blood culture results and chest imaging for pulmonary septic emboli were not disclosed, the documented metastatic infection sites in a hemodialysis patient with typical tricuspid valve involvement strongly support the final diagnosis.
